title: Widen the ground-truth harness before it measures the repair
description:
## The measuring stick has two known faults

`ground-truth.yml` is what tl-4jg reads to declare the repair done. Two of its checks are
wrong in ways that matter, per spec lines 512-515:

1. **The duplication check omits gender from its key.** It reports **176** duplicate
   groups where the true figure is **98**. The 176 decomposes into 40 cross-gender
   collisions (real, distinct fixtures — 39 of the 40 carry different scores), 42 phantoms,
   and 94 genuine two-perspective rows. A repair validated against 176 would look like it
   destroyed data when it had not, or worse, invite a "fix" that collapses the 40 real
   fixtures.

2. **The identity check reproduces only `_ilike_pattern`** — one of the five matchers in
   `apps/api`, and not the one `/api/stats/team` uses. It therefore under-reports the
   identity defect, and specifically misses that FHSU (12/150) and RSU (47/132) are among
   the worst-affected programmes.

## Fix

Add gender to the duplication key. Run the identity check against all five matchers, or
against the canon once tl-ath lands.

## Acceptance

The duplication check reports 98 groups on the current database, not 176. The identity
check reports per-matcher figures that reproduce the FHSU 12/150 and RSU 47/132
measurements.

title: Fix SideArm rosters labelled with each other's team in 723 games (gh-21)
description:
GitHub issue #21.

## Mechanism

`parse_sidearm_game` swaps `home_team`/`away_team` (and scores, and the abbrev map) when the header hint disagrees with the score table, and correctly rebuilds `team_game_stats` from the corrected triple afterwards. **It never reorders the player tables.** So in every swapped game each roster carries the other team's name.

## Acceptance

The swap goes **723 → 0** on the arithmetic gate and **739 → 0** against the HTML captions. StatCrew stays at 0/337.

title: Backfill is_conference_game — gender-aware and season-aware
description:
## The field has always been NULL

ADR-006 claims `is_conference_game` is populated from SideArm's `is_conference` flag. That is false and was never implemented — no file under `packages/pipeline/src` reads the flag, and the column is NULL for **2,140 of 2,140** rows. (The `is_conference` values in cached pages belong to a scoreboard sidebar widget, not to the game being parsed.) See ADR-006's superseding note.

So it is **derived**, from `schools.toml` GAC membership per ADR-007.

## Three constraints, each of which changes the answer

**1. Gender-aware.** Measured: gender-aware 1,430 conference rows against gender-blind 1,533 — **103 false positives**, every one a real fixture where an institution fields the other gender outside the GAC (28 men's vs Okla. Baptist, 24 women's vs Northeastern St., 16 women's vs Newman, 11 women's vs Rogers State).

**2. Season-aware.** Men's GAC is HU/OBU/SNU for 2016-2018 and gains FHSU/NU/NSU/RSU from 2019; women's is a stable seven throughout. Add a `(gender, institution_slug, since_year)` membership table and a `gac_since` field to schools.toml so this derives from config, not a hardcoded table in the loader.

**3. Corrected own-team identification.** None of the five apps/api matchers is good enough — canon.json is a prerequisite.

## The membership question is settled

Resolved 2026-08-07 and recorded in the spec: `schools.toml` is a membership record, not a scrape-coverage list. Meeting frequency separates a member from a neighbour by an order of magnitude (known GAC 3.33–4.24 meetings per programme per season vs Northeastern State 0.51, Newman 0.30, Rogers State 0.29), and 100% of the women's Northeastern State fixtures fall in Aug–Sep against 40% for GAC opponents. These are out-of-conference friendlies against nearby institutions.

Men's affiliates show the same signature inverted: FHSU 1.0 → 32.0 meetings/season at exactly 2019, against a flat 16.7 → 13.4 for OBU (member throughout). Corroborates docs/UI_DESIGN.md:18. **Pre-2019 men's fixtures against FHSU/NU/NSU/RSU are non-conference.**

## Ships as

A migration plus a loader change, so it stays populated.

## Acceptance

`is_conference_game` non-NULL for all rows, derived gender-aware and season-aware, zero rows resolving to two programmes.

title: Verify the repair — before/after for every named defect
description:
## What

Re-run both Keelson validation workflows and record before/after counts for **every**
defect in the spec's Problem Statement table. These numbers become the S2 Feed Health
board's first baseline.

```
keelson workflow run data-integrity --project ed-insights-platform
keelson workflow run ground-truth   --project ed-insights-platform
```

## Acceptance

- The full re-parse harness reports **2,098/2,098** games re-parsed with 0 errors and 0
  field diffs. *(Not 2,140 — tl-o23 deletes 42 phantom games and their cached HTML, so the
  post-repair corpus is smaller. The spec carries the stale 2,140 figure at line 727 and
  needs the same correction.)*
- `ground-truth.yml` reports no alarms it did not report before the repair
- Every acceptance number from **every** sibling task is independently confirmed here, not
  self-reported by the task that made the change — including the parquet purge (tl-3zm) and
  the shots-on-goal fix (tl-ce3)
- The measuring stick itself has been widened first (tl-gtw), or the baseline is measured
  with a known-broken instrument

title: GATE — validate --year 2026 against live schedule pages for all 13 programmes
description:
## This is a hard gate, and it is time-boxed

The D2 season starts around **27 August 2026**. `schools.toml` has **no 2026 entry for any programme**, so `--year 2026` is doing all the work with no validation behind it. Every one of the thirteen schedule pages needs a manual dry run before kickoff.

## The specific failure being guarded against

A SideArm site serving 2025 instead of an empty 2026 page **reproduces the FHSU/OBU corruption on day one** — that is exactly how the 42 phantom rows were created.

T-redirect-assert is the guard that catches it, and it must be in place before this gate runs, because during preseason the year-segment assertion alone is blind.

## Acceptance

All 13 enabled programmes produce either a valid empty 2026 schedule or valid 2026 fixtures. Any page that 302s or serves a different season is caught and named. Run this **before** turning the wall clock on.

title: src/canon.ts — the identity map with NSU reconstruction
description:
## What

Build the identity map from `SELECT DISTINCT` over `team` / `home_team` / `away_team`, **keyed on abbreviation, never name** — the live schools table has two rows literally named "Harding".

Consumes the adjudicated `canon.json` from T-identity-canon rather than re-deriving it.

## The NSU reconstruction path

NSU is `enabled=false` because their site is a KnockoutJS SPA with no scraper — but every box score records **both** rosters, so their conference record is recoverable from the six schools they played.

This is honest but lossy, and the boards must say so: their *conference* record is exact; any match against a non-GAC opponent nobody else played is invisible, so their *overall* record is not recoverable. A conference-only table including NSU is honest; an overall table including NSU is not.

## Acceptance

A table correct for all seven men's programmes including reconstructed NSU, and all seven women's programmes (which need no reconstruction). Absorbs "Okla. Baptist" / "Oklahoma Baptist" / "Okla. Baptist OKLA." and "#16 Northeastern State".

title: S0.5 — Repair the existing data
description:
The numbers in ed_insights are true; the labels are wrong. Ground-truth validation established 2,140/2,140 games re-parse exactly and 493/493 fixtures agree on score across two unrelated websites — but home/away, roster attribution and card type are fabricated or inverted. All of it is repairable offline from the 1.1 GB of cached HTML already on disk. No re-scrape required.

Nothing downstream is worth building until this lands: a prettier dashboard over inverted records is a downgrade.

Spec: docs/specs/touchline-rib.md#S0.5. Decision: ADR-008, D-02 (correctness before presentation), D-03 (repair what we have).

title: Package skeleton from keelson-rib-workiq
description:
Copy the workiq skeleton **verbatim** — it is the smallest reference rib and the least likely to carry assumptions we do not want.

`src/index.ts` default-exports a Rib with exactly one tool (`touchline_query`).

## Proves

Discovery finds the rib, activation does not throw, `keelson rib list` shows it. Nothing more — this is the "does the harness accept us" gate, deliberately separated from any real logic.

title: src/wallclock.ts with last-fired.json
description:
`setInterval(60_000).unref()` evaluating a slot table against local time: Sun 06:00, Wed 06:00, Sat 22:00, Fri 16:00 check-only, plus a matchday 20:00–23:59 window every 30 minutes.

Persists `last-fired.json` so a restart neither double-fires nor skips. Calls `ctx.refreshWorkflow('touchline-refresh')` — **not** `ctx.runWorkflow`.

## Acknowledged risk

This runs inside the Keelson server process and shells out to `uv run` in a git checkout on a timer. Nothing in the rib contract forbids it and both chamber and squad hold timers — but nothing in Keelson tests that path either, and a bug there is a bug in the harness. That is why the launchd fallback ships **alongside** it, not instead of it (D-05).

title: S1 — The canon and the first Observation
description:
New repo: **github.com/ed-insights-ai/keelson-rib-touchline**. Package skeleton copied
verbatim from keelson-rib-workiq.

The structural bet: `scripts/load_db.py:186-201` DELETEs then re-INSERTs every child row
per game_id on each load, so Postgres has no memory — last week's numbers are physically
gone. Touchline writes one immutable Observation JSON per refresh carrying **full
per-match box lines** (~2 MB, ~55 MB a season, per D-01's fat-ledger decision), which
makes "what moved since Saturday" a diff between two files rather than a query nobody
can answer.

Nothing renders at this stage. The ledger *is* the product; everything downstream is a
projection of it.

Spec: docs/specs/touchline-rib.md#S1. Can run parallel to S0.

title: bin/observe.ts — write the first immutable Observation
description:
## What it writes

One immutable Observation JSON per refresh. Per **D-01 (fat ledger)** it stores **full
per-match box lines**, not just derived season state: the canonical table, per-team
aggregates, per-player season lines, the full box line for every match, a
`game_id → fingerprint` map, and provenance.

Roughly **2 MB per observation, ~55 MB for a season** (measured at 2.85 MB once both
genders are in scope per D-04).

## Do not build the thin version

A ~200 KB derived-state-only ledger is the design D-01 explicitly **rejected**. It makes
"show me the Sep 6 table" work but leaves "what did we think that match's shot count was
on Sep 6" unanswerable, and it limits the score-mutation integrity check to scores only —
a silent shot-count correction would pass unnoticed. 55 MB is not a constraint on any
machine we care about, and the checks we cannot imagine yet are the ones we will want in
October.

**Revisit only if:** observation write time exceeds ~10s, or a collector's read time
becomes visible in board latency.

## The rule that makes everything else work

**Exactly one thing touches Postgres, once per refresh: `bin/observe.ts`.** No board, no
collector, no tool ever queries the database. Every board is then a pure function of files
on disk — fast, deterministic, testable, offline, and instantly recomposable.

## What it unlocks

- "What moved since Saturday" is a diff between two files
- Four of the nine integrity checks compare two observations
- "Show me the table as it stood on September 6th" is just reading an older file
- A watermark gate reads the diff before spending a turn — a quiet Tuesday costs zero tokens

## Acceptance

An observation lands on disk carrying full per-match box lines, with a table correct for
all fourteen programmes. Read-only against a schema the rib does not own (ADR-008 — no DDL
on ed_insights, ever).

title: The complete 7-node touchline-refresh
description:
The full DAG including the scrape node, with the season-label assertion.

## Four modes, switched by reading the fixture calendar

- **Preseason** — one 06:00 daily pull that mostly discovers nothing, which is exactly what you want it doing before it matters
- **In-season quiet** — 06:00 Sun and Wed. Identical-content skip means "updated 2 days ago" is honest rather than restamped
- **Matchday** — at 20:00 the wall clock notices fixtures dated today and polls every 30 minutes, always `--no-cache`. Within ~30 minutes of a final whistle the score is in the header, the table has re-sorted with a new Δ, form badges shifted, and the slate card flipped. **This is the moment the design exists for.**
- **Dispatch** — runs if and only if the watermark says something landed and the fingerprint says the table moved

## Workflow authoring notes

Bash nodes read upstream output via `KEELSON_NODE_<id>_OUTPUT` env, **not** `$<id>.output`. A workflow's `name` must equal its filename stem. Watch column-1 content inside block scalars — an embedded heredoc at column 1 terminates the scalar and silently unregisters the workflow.

title: Build the authoritative opponent-string identity map (canon.json)
description:
## Why this is first

Every other repair keys on "which programme is this row about?" and the five matchers in apps/api all answer it differently. This task produces one answer, checked in as `canon.json`, consumed by both the S0.5 migration and the rib's `src/canon.ts`.

## What to build

A map from every DISTINCT opponent string across `team` / `home_team` / `away_team` to `(institution_slug, gender)` — keyed on **abbreviation, never name** (the live schools table has two rows literally named "Harding").

Must absorb the real messiness: "Okla. Baptist" / "Oklahoma Baptist" / "Okla. Baptist OKLA.", and ranked-team prefixes like "#16 Northeastern State".

## The 13 near-misses — hand adjudication required

Resolution is unambiguous but not automatic. No opponent string resolves to two programmes, so there are no ties to break. But 13 distinct strings are near-misses and getting them wrong is **silent**:

- MUST resolve (real GAC programmes under alternate spellings): "Northwestern OSU" (3 rows), "Southwestern OSU" (2 rows)
- MUST NOT resolve (not members): "Southwest Baptist" (24 rows), "Dallas Baptist", "Williams Baptist", "Southwestern Christi.", "Southwestern (KS)", "Central Baptist"

Bake the adjudicated list into `canon.json`, **not** into the migration.

## Gender is a separate axis

Opponent strings carry no gender, so the map goes to a **gender-free institution slug** with gender supplied separately from `schools.gender` of the row's `school_id` (reliable: all 2,140 rows agree with the mens-soccer/womens-soccer segment of their own source_url).

## Acceptance

- Every DISTINCT opponent string resolves or is explicitly marked non-member
- Zero strings resolve to two programmes
- The 13 near-misses each carry a written adjudication in the file
- `canon.json` is committed to this repo and readable by the rib

title: Migration 005 deletes all data in both directions, and runs on every start (gh-19)
description:
GitHub issue #19.

## Mechanism

`apps/api/alembic/versions/005_reset_gac_schools.py` unconditionally deletes every row from all five data tables — in **both** `upgrade()` and `downgrade()`.

There is no safe direction to run it. Combined with a container that runs migrations on every start, this is a loaded gun pointed at the database that all the S0.5 repair work is about to land in.

## Why P0 despite not being a data-quality bug

Doing the repair work first and *then* discovering this wipes it would be the single worst outcome available. Fix it before T-verify-repair records any baseline.

## Acceptance

No alembic revision deletes data unconditionally. Migrations on startup are either removed or provably non-destructive.

title: S4 — The refresh DAG and the wall clock
description:
Scheduled freshness end to end, unattended, against the project checkout — the requirement the harness heartbeat structurally cannot meet.

**Keelson has no cron.** No `schedule:`, `cron:` or `every:` field exists anywhere in the workflow YAML schema. Freshness is assembled from three real clocks, and one obvious-looking seam is a trap:

- **[A] The harness heartbeat** — 30s tick in `apps/server/src/scheduler.ts` re-runs any bound producer with a `cadenceMs`. Always fires with empty inputs and KEELSON_HOME as cwd. Drives the cheap board collectors, which need neither.
- **[B] A rib-held wall clock** — `setInterval(60_000).unref()` evaluating a slot table against local time. The only in-process way to get time-of-day.
- **[C] A launchd fallback** — `keelson workflow run touchline-refresh --no-watch --json --base-url http://127.0.0.1:7878`. The `--base-url` forces it through the running server so it publishes the bound key exactly like [B].
- **[TRAP] `ctx.runWorkflow`** — the only seam that accepts a cwd, which is why two of three design proposals chose it. It writes no run row, fires no run event, and **does not publish to a bound snapshot key** (bindings are keyed by definition object identity; `runDefinition` parses a fresh object). A refresh through it reaches the database and never reaches the screen. cwd was never load-bearing anyway — every bash node already cds into the checkout.

Spec: docs/specs/touchline-rib.md#S4.

title: S2 — Feed Health, the first board
description:
All nine integrity checks with evidence and causing `file:line`, rendered as the first board shipped — before anything pretty.

On a dataset with this many named defects, the panel that says which numbers are lying and cites the line that broke them is the highest value-per-hour work available. **If the project stopped here it would still have delivered the most important thing.**

Spec: docs/specs/touchline-rib.md#S2. Depends on S1 — four of the nine checks compare two observations.

title: Close the preseason blind spot in the season assertion
description:
## The residual gap PR #14 left

FHSU and OBU men's soccer have no season slug `2020` — their COVID season was played in spring 2021 and is slugged `2020-21` — so `/schedule/2020` 302s to the bare `/schedule`, which serves **whatever season is current**. That is how 42 rows dated 2025 came to be filed under 2020.

PR #14's year-segment assertion *would* have prevented these 42, but it is **blind during preseason**: when the fallback page has no box scores yet, the code takes the `if not matches` branch and logs the same message for "season not started" and "you were served a different season".

Today is preseason. This is exactly the window where the guard does not work.

## Fix

Add a redirect assertion (`resp.history` / `resp.url`) alongside the year-segment check — correct in both windows.

Also remove the unreachable `2020` entries from FHSU's and OBU's `years` in schools.toml, **or** widen the slug type: `discover_sidearm_season(year: int, ...)` cannot express `2020-21`.

## Why it blocks the phantom deletion

Deleting the poisoned cache directories without this guard means the next scrape re-ingests them.

## Acceptance

A scrape of a season slug that 302s to a different season fails loudly, naming the season actually served — and does so when the served page has zero box scores.

title: Add player-team attribution to player_game_stats (gh-22)
description:
GitHub issue #22.

## Mechanism

`player_game_stats.school_id` is the **scraping** school, not the player's team, and the schema has no player-team foreign key — only a free-text `team` varchar. Every per-school player query keys on `school_id` alone and therefore returns **both rosters of every game that school scraped**.

## Fix

The attribution must be correct before it is stored, so this depends on the roster swap being fixed first — otherwise we would faithfully persist the wrong team.

## Acceptance

Every per-school player endpoint returns exactly one roster. Verified against a game where both teams are GAC members (both perspectives exist and must agree).

title: src/integrity.ts — nine checks with evidence and file:line
description:
Nine checks. Four of them are cross-observation and are impossible without the ledger: did a game_id change identity, did a final score mutate, did a programme lose matches, is the feed stale.

Each check reports **evidence and the causing file:line**, not just a pass/fail. The two Keelson workflows already in `.keelson/workflows/` (data-integrity.yml, ground-truth.yml) are the reference implementations — port their logic rather than re-deriving it.

title: touchline-refresh in observe-only form
description:
The workflow contribution with the scrape node **omitted** — it observes the database as it currently stands and publishes Feed Health.

Separating this from the full DAG (S4) means the board is live and trustworthy before anything is allowed to write to the database on a timer.

title: Fix fabricated home/away in both parsers (gh-20)
description:
GitHub issue #20.

## Mechanism

Both parsers force the scraping school into the home slot, by two different routes. Correct in only **651 of 1,745** SideArm games (37%).

## Evidence

- 471 of 569 twice-scraped fixtures have **both** rows claiming home — a logical impossibility that proves the field is invented, not observed
- `home_team='Harding'` is 337/337 for HU+HUW; should be roughly half

## Fix

Derive home/away from the **source venue**, not from row order or the scraping school. Recoverable offline from cached HTML — no re-scrape.

## Why this is P0

It is the top of the dependency chain. gh-15 (five matchers) is pointless while `home_team` itself is fabricated 63% of the time, and the fail-open matcher in `conferences.py` reads the opponent's score as our own when identification fails.

## Acceptance

Cross-perspective home/away contradictions go **471 → 0** across the 569 two-perspective fixtures. `home_team='Harding'` falls from 337/337 to roughly half.

title: Create keelson-rib-touchline on the ed-insights-ai organization
description:
## Hard requirement

The repo **MUST** be created under the `ed-insights-ai` organization — never a personal account. This is a standing constraint from the user, not a preference.

`gh repo create ed-insights-ai/keelson-rib-touchline --private`

## Also set up

- CI matching the ed-insights-platform conventions (lint + typecheck + test)
- CONTRIBUTING.md, checked before any PR is opened against it
- Branch protection consistent with the platform repo

title: bin/collect-feed.ts and the pressbox surface
description:
The bound collector plus the `pressbox` surface. Pressbox stays **single and gender-spanning** — unlike the season surfaces, feed health is about the pipeline, not about a competition.

Region keys carry no gender segment here.

title: Delete the 42 phantom rows and their poisoned cache directories (gh-26)
description:
GitHub issue #26.

## They are duplicates, not mislabels

FHSU 2020 (24 rows) and OBU 2020 (18 rows), all carrying `/stats/2025/` source URLs.
Measured: **42/42 have a 2025 twin** matching on source_url, both team names and both
scores. Children match too — 1,604 player lines, 84 team lines, 321 events. There is
nothing to relabel and nothing to recover, so the repair is DELETE.

## The cache directories must go with them

`data/raw_html/fhsu/2020/` and `obu/2020/` are **not** empty: 42 files, every one the
2025 season. FHSU's 24 are byte-identical by SHA-1 to `2025/`; OBU's 18 differ only in
a cache-buster `<script>`. A scan of every cached `*/2020` directory flags exactly these
two and no others.

## What deleting them fixes

The only real aggregate inflation in the database. `/api/stats/players` groups by
`school_id` without `season_year`, so **574 (player, school) rows currently carry
doubled totals**.

## DO NOT delete anything the season-year detector merely flags

A COVID season played in spring is filed under the previous year and is **correct**.
There are **79 legitimate rows** with `season_year=2020` dated 2021 across nine
programmes. The detector must be the one from gh-23/`ground-truth.yml:558`:

```sql
extract(year from date) NOT IN (season_year, season_year + 1)
```

Verified: that formula returns exactly **42** rows. Dropping the `+ 1` returns 121 and
sweeps up all 79 real games. Pin the DELETE to the 42 rows with a verified 2025 twin —
match on source_url, both team names and both scores — not to the detector's output.

The genuine 2020 seasons are missing, not corrupt, and are out of scope.

## Acceptance

- Exactly 42 games rows plus their children are gone; the 79 spring-2021 rows are untouched
- Both poisoned cache directories are gone
- `extract(year from date) NOT IN (season_year, season_year+1)` returns **0** rows
- Doubled-aggregate count **574 → 0**

title: Scrape reports success on partial and rejected runs (gh-17)
description:
GitHub issue #17.

## Root cause

The scrape CLI's success signal does not reflect whether the data it produced is complete. Surfaced by the review loop on PR #14; both findings were correctly judged out of scope there.

## Why it becomes load-bearing

At S4 the refresh DAG runs unattended on a wall clock. A scrape that half-fails and exits 0 leaves the boards showing yesterday's numbers presented as current — which the v1 Definition of Done explicitly forbids.

## Acceptance

A partial or fully-rejected scrape exits non-zero and names what was missing. Exit codes are a stable contract the launchd job and the workflow both read.

title: Add the canonical match key column
description:
## What

`sha1(gender | date | sorted normalized institution pair)` as a column on `games`, populated by the loader.

## Gender is not optional in the key

Without it, **40 pairs of genuinely distinct fixtures collide** — a men's and a women's match on the same date between the same two institutions — and **39 of those 40 carry different scores**, so collapsing them would silently destroy a real result. An early draft of this task omitted gender and would have stripped 17/17 games from SWOSU and 11/11 from SNUW.

## The pair must be sorted, never (home, away)

Home/away is fabricated (see T-home-away), so an order-dependent key would fail to match the two perspectives of the same fixture.

## Do NOT de-duplicate

The two-perspective rows are the only free correctness oracle in the dataset and are the regression test for the roster swap and home/away defects. Each group collapses into one match with **two source perspectives** — strictly better than picking a winner, because two schools' box scores sometimes disagree on *shots* even when they agree on the score.

## Expected shape (1,987 keyable rows, phantoms already gone)

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| distinct canonical matches | 1,401 |
| two-perspective fixtures | 586 (men 204, women 382) |
| max group size | 2 |
| groups where count(*) != count(DISTINCT school_id) | 0 |
| groups mixing genders | 0 |
| groups disagreeing on oriented score | 0 |

## Residual risk

A same-gender doubleheader between the same two institutions on one date would collide. Zero such cases exist 2016-2025. Mitigation if one appears: append the site-unique numeric boxscore id from the URL.

## Acceptance

Every group has count(*) = count(DISTINCT school_id), max size 2, zero gender mixing, zero oriented-score disagreement. Currently 40 violations, all phantom, so 0 after T-phantoms.

title: Fix 111 games with NULL date and venue='NaN' (gh-24)
description:
GitHub issue #24.

## Mechanism

One over-strict title regex at `packages/pipeline/src/parser.py:159` accepts only one of three date/venue title forms. The other two fall through, leaving `date` NULL and `venue` as the literal string 'NaN'.

## Why this blocks the canonical key

111 rows have no date and therefore cannot receive a `(gender, date, sorted pair)` key. This must land before T-canonical-key.

## Acceptance

`date IS NULL` goes **111 → 0** and `venue='NaN'` goes **111 → 0**.

title: src/keys.ts and src/gates.ts — the shared key and gate helpers
description:
Named in the Component Inventory (spec :352, :354) and assumed by several later tasks, but
assigned to no stage.

`src/keys.ts` owns region-key construction — including the `:m:`/`:w:` gender segment, so the
two season surfaces cannot drift apart by hand-built strings. tl-tre's boot self-check asserts
a producer key equals its region key; both sides should be built by this one module or the
check is comparing two independent spellings of the same intent.

`src/gates.ts` owns the watermark and fingerprint gates that decide whether a refresh is worth
spending a turn on. A quiet Tuesday costing zero tokens is a property of this file.

title: bin/collect-ledger.ts — the Observation Ledger board
description:
## The sixth collector

The Component Inventory (spec :349) requires six bound collectors. Five have tasks — feed,
table, slate, race, form. This is the missing one.

## What it renders

The pressbox **Observation Ledger** region on a 60m cadence (spec :419): the last twenty
observations, a cumulative-matches staircase chart of the season's scraping, and the diff
between any two observations.

This is the board that makes the structural bet visible. By December it holds ~24
observations and the staircase shows every week the scraper ran — flat steps and all.

## Why it cannot be skipped

tl-tre's boot self-check asserts that every cadence-bearing region has a matching bound
producer whose key equals the region key. A pressbox surface declaring a Ledger region with
no `collect-ledger` producer **throws at boot** — this is precisely the failure class that
check exists to catch.

## Acceptance

The Ledger region renders the last twenty observations and the cumulative staircase, and
the boot self-check passes with the pressbox surface fully populated.

title: Stop the loader writing literal 'NaN' into nullable text columns (gh-25)
description:
GitHub issue #25.

## Mechanism

`packages/pipeline/scripts/load_db.py:236-247` (`_events_row`) uses bare `row.get(...)` for nullable text columns, while every numeric column in the same file goes through `_int_or_none` / `_bool_or_none`. Pandas `np.nan` is adapted by psycopg2 and lands as the literal three-character text `'NaN'` rather than SQL NULL.

Same root cause as the `venue='NaN'` half of gh-24, different code path.

## Acceptance

Zero occurrences of the literal string 'NaN' in any nullable text column across game_events, games and player_game_stats.

title: S5 — Tools and chat ◆ v1
description:
**This epic is v1.** Cheapest stage, highest usefulness-to-code ratio.

Twelve tools registered once become available in three places: the Keelson composer, inside workflow prompt nodes, and over `POST /api/mcp` to Claude Code, Copilot or Codex. Ten of the twelve are read-only (`state_changing: false`) so they reach MCP by default.

v1 is: correct data, a trustworthy health panel, live boards, scheduled refresh, and a season you can ask questions about.

Spec: docs/specs/touchline-rib.md#S5. Depends on S1 — the ledger is what every tool reads.

title: Purge 712 retired-ordinal rows from exported parquets (gh-27)
description:
GitHub issue #27.

## Mechanism

`src/storage.py:112-140` (`merge_all_schools`) concatenates whatever season directories are
on disk and never prunes rows whose school ordinal is no longer configured.
`scripts/export.py:36` then copies the result to `data/`.

The loader escapes it only by an accident of directory naming (`scripts/load_db.py:31-33`
skips the `all` dir), so nothing in the pipeline ever notices.

## Why it matters anyway

CLAUDE.md documents the stale figures (18 schools / 2,852 games) that this file produces,
and anyone reading `data/*.parquet` instead of Postgres gets them.

## Second half — do not drop this

gh-27 also covers a real data-loss bug in the same file: **`_build_event_id` omits
`description` from the identity**, so distinct events collide and **28 real events are lost
at merge time, including 1 goal**. Plus the `export-staleness` check and the
`merge_all_seasons` / `merge_all_schools` non-numeric-slug reconciliation.

## Acceptance

- `data/structured/all/games.parquet` carries 0 rows from retired school ordinals; its
  counts match Postgres
- Lost events go **28 → 0**, including the goal
- The export-staleness check passes

title: season-men and season-women surfaces
description:
## Why two surfaces

A surface declares **static** region keys, so `rib:touchline:table` is men's or women's,
never both. There is no runtime toggle available.

Region keys carry a gender segment: `rib:touchline:m:table`, `rib:touchline:w:table`.

## Why not defer women's

D-04 was overturned 2026-08-07. The premise that men's was the better-supported half is
**factually false**: women's has 1,238 games to men's 902, zero phantom rows to 42, one
parse blob to 33, and a complete seven-team round robin every season since 2016.

The original deferral also rested on a claim that does not survive measurement — that
"every school carrying the identity defect is a women's programme, the men's side is
clean." That is true only of `_ilike_pattern`, which is one of five matchers and is *not*
the one `/api/stats/team` uses. Under the full-name ILIKE at `stats.py:44-49` the two
worst-affected programmes after the women's are **men's**: FHSU identifies itself in 12
of 150 games, RSU in 47 of 132. Deferring women's would not have avoided the identity
defect; it would have hidden half of it.

title: Recover 166 SideArm red cards stored as yellow (gh-23)
description:
GitHub issue #23.

## Mechanism

The card type is encoded **only** as a CSS class on an empty `<td>` — `penalty-type red` —
which the parser never reads, so every SideArm card is stored as yellow.

## This is one change, not two

D-03 moved the parser fix **into the repair pass**: it is a regex change plus a re-parse.
Splitting the backfill from the parser change would leave every card in the 2026 season
stored as yellow until November, and would make the S0.5 verification gate unsatisfiable —
a re-parse with the still-hardcoded parser either reverts the backfill or reports 166
field diffs.

So this task is both halves:

1. Read the card type from the `penalty-type` CSS class at `sidearm_parser.py:339-348`
   instead of hardcoding yellow.
2. Re-parse the cached HTML to backfill the historical 166. No re-scrape needed — the
   class is present in every cached page.

## Acceptance

- Card type is read from the `penalty-type` CSS class, **not hardcoded** (gh-23)
- `penalty-type red` markers in cached HTML = 166 and SideArm `red_card` rows = 166
  (currently 166 markers against 43 stored reds)
- A fresh parse of any cached page reproduces its stored card types exactly, so the
  S0.5 re-parse harness reports 0 field diffs on card columns

title: S0 — Pipeline hardening
description:
The destructive defects, and the ones that make a run lie about its own success. PR #14 (season assertion + merge safety) and PR #18 (repo growth) already landed; this epic is the residue.

Spec: docs/specs/touchline-rib.md#S0.

title: The twelve tools
description:
All twelve, with `state_changing: false` on the ten read-only ones so they are MCP-reachable by default.

Note the design constraint that killed the obvious alternative: a **bash node cannot publish a snapshot** — it is a subprocess with no snapshot manager, no rib context and no module state. All three original design proposals got this wrong. The write path is an in-process tool named in the prompt node's tool whitelist, which is exactly how chamber does it.

title: bin/collect-slate.ts — fixtures and results
description:
The slate card flips from fixture to result within ~30 minutes of a final whistle, with nobody clicking anything.

Distinct workflow name, own `expectView` validator.

title: The in-process Matchday composer
description:
Fold the Matchday panel and the record still reads 4-1-2 in the header strip — the board header carries the story even collapsed. That is the design contract, not a detail.

Also the point at which to **confirm the board-chart colour break**: Keelson board charts cannot use literal hex, so the Ed Insights teal/orange contract survives on HTML pages but not on board charts. Decide here whether the season-arc chart stays on a board or moves entirely to HTML.

title: bin/collect-table.ts — the standings board
description:
Bound contribution with a distinct workflow name and an `expectView` validator.

Proves the heartbeat re-runs bound producers with zero scheduling code, and that boards render from disk in milliseconds.

Seven programmes, not six — the row for reconstructed NSU says so rather than omitting a real member.
notes:
## Ships gender-doubled

D-04 puts both genders in scope, and a surface declares **static** region keys — so this
collector ships twice, writing `rib:touchline:m:*` and `rib:touchline:w:*` slot files. Two
slot files, not one with a gender column. That is D-04's stated cost and it is not optional.

title: S3 — The Table and The Slate
description:
The first visible payoff of the structural bet: a real Δ against a real prior observation.

Two bound collectors, the `season-men` and `season-women` surfaces, and the in-process Matchday composer.

Spec: docs/specs/touchline-rib.md#S3.

title: The launchd fallback plist
description:
`keelson workflow run touchline-refresh --no-watch --json --base-url http://127.0.0.1:7878`

Belt and suspenders, because a laptop sleeps. The `--base-url` forces it through the running server so it publishes the bound key. Exit codes are a stable contract.

OS-supervised and one file — but it gives up matchday awareness, because a plist cannot read the fixture calendar and decide it should poll tonight. Hence both, per D-05.

title: Boot self-check — every cadence-bearing region has a matching bound producer
description:
## Why

A surface declares static region keys. A region with a cadence but no bound producer whose key **equals** the region key renders empty forever, silently — and the failure looks like "no data yet" rather than a wiring bug.

Assert the invariant at boot and throw. Cheap, and it catches the whole class.

title: Unify the five inconsistent team matchers (gh-15, widened)
description:
GitHub issue #15 — **scoped to `_ilike_pattern` only and needs widening to all five**.

## The five implementations

`conferences.py`, `teams.py`, `stats.py`, `players.py`, `insights.py` — five implementations, no shared helper. The worst offender is the full-name ILIKE at `stats.py:44-49`, which `/api/stats/team` uses.

## The fail-open mechanism

```python
is_home = _matches_pattern(g.home_team, pattern)
own_score = g.home_score if is_home else g.away_score
opp_score = g.away_score if is_home else g.home_score
```

There is no third branch. A match **failure** is indistinguishable from "we are the away team" — so the opponent's score is silently read as our own. `_ilike_pattern` cannot identify a school in 164 scored games.

## Sequencing

Blocked by T-home-away: there is no point fixing how the API reads `home_team` while `home_team` itself is fabricated in 63% of rows. Also blocked by T-identity-canon — the fix should adopt the one canonical matcher, not invent a sixth.

## Acceptance

One shared matcher, used by all five routers. A match failure raises or returns an explicit unknown — never falls through to the away branch. 651 wrong rows in stats.py alone go to 0.

title: API correctness
description: The FastAPI service answers "which programme is this row about?" five different ways in five files, none of them shared. The rib's canon supersedes all five for rib purposes, but apps/web reads the API directly and gets the wrong answers today.

title: The pressbox Archive region
description:
Spec :420. The dated index of everything the rib has published — dispatches, match pages,
observations — so the season reads as a bound volume rather than a folder.

Cadence-bearing, so it needs a bound producer whose key matches its region key or tl-tre's boot
self-check throws.

title: touchline-scout — the Thursday opponent workflow
description:
Spec :386. Four parallel prompt nodes, Thursday 17:00 — the scouting pass on the weekend's
fixtures.

Distinct from tl-7c2's `/scout <abbr>` slash command, which is the on-demand single-team
lookup. This is the scheduled sweep that has a report waiting before you ask for it.

title: touchline-retry-errors — recover the 34 orphaned error blobs
description:
Spec :387. `data/errors/` holds 34 parse blobs that failed and were never retried. Nothing
in the pipeline ever looks at them again, so a transient fetch failure is indistinguishable
from a page that genuinely cannot be parsed.

A workflow that re-attempts them on a cadence turns that pile into either recovered matches or
a known, bounded list of genuinely-unparseable pages — which is a Feed Health line rather than
a silent gap.

Note the gender asymmetry already measured: 33 of the 34 are men's, 1 is women's.

title: S7 — The Race
description:
The fun. Odds that move every Saturday, and a swing table that turns other people's games into your games.

**The biggest game left on the schedule isn't on the schedule** — that is the reason to open the tab on a Sunday morning, and nothing in the existing stack can compute it.

Depends on enough conference matches for shrunk rates to mean anything. Spec: docs/specs/touchline-rib.md#S7.

title: src/pages.ts + src/tools/emit.ts — the in-process publish seam
description: Plus boot reconciliation from `<dataHome>/pages/` so published pages survive a restart.

title: The touchline-dispatch gate/author/publish DAG
description: The cost gates are the point: the dispatch runs if and only if the watermark says something landed **and** the fingerprint says the table moved. A week where nothing moved spends nothing.

title: /table, /scout <abbr>, /dispatch
description: `/scout` takes an abbreviation with roster completion — abbreviation, never name, for the same reason canon.ts is keyed that way.

title: S6 — The Match Page and the Dispatch
description:
Once a week the rib publishes a dated, versioned HTML page into Keelson's full-width drawer — the thing you would actually send someone.

The layout is a **deterministic function of the ledger**; only the prose is generated, slotted into a fixed scaffold so the archive stays a series instead of being silently redesigned every week. (A 262 KB page cannot round-trip through a tool result anyway.)

Ships after kickoff on purpose — it benefits most from a month of trustworthy data underneath it. This is the phasing call the design brief flagged as genuinely arguable: the counter-case is that the broadsheet is what decides whether this feels like a product or a dashboard.

Spec: docs/specs/touchline-rib.md#S6.

title: Stop coercing missing shots_on_goal to 0 (gh-29)
description:
GitHub issue #29.

## Mechanism

`packages/pipeline/src/parser.py:886-888` coerces a missing shots-on-goal value to 0 rather
than leaving it NULL, for a column the source does not have — producing 12 impossible rows
(goals > shots on goal).

## Second half — do not drop this

gh-29 also covers the `rsplit(None, 1)` fix: **3 mangled abbreviations produce all-zero
stat rows**. And a consumer audit for the NULL handling.

## Note — this is a breaking change

0 → NULL changes the meaning of an existing column. Anything summing or averaging it
changes answer. Decide the migration story before shipping and flag it to the user if
consumers are affected — this is the one task in S0.5 whose fix is not purely additive.

## Acceptance

- Zero rows where goals > shots_on_goal; missing values are NULL, not 0
- The 3 mangled abbreviations parse correctly and no longer produce all-zero stat rows
- Every consumer of `shots_on_goal` has been audited for NULL handling

title: contributeDocs — make the rib self-describing
description: So `keelson_docs` returns Touchline's own contract. An agent that has never seen the rib can discover what it can do without reading its source.

title: touchline_refresh as a durable op
description: So a refresh survives a server restart mid-run and a half-failed refresh leaves the panel reading **stale**, never yesterday's numbers presented as current. That is an explicit v1 Definition-of-Done requirement.

title: The forbidden-metric render gate
description:
Refuse to publish prose containing `xG`, `possession`, `pass` or `foul` tokens — `team_game_stats` has exactly ten columns and **none of them are those**. A narrator that invents plausible soccer metrics we do not measure is worse than no narrator.

The author node's `allowed_tools` grants only Touchline tools, which at the SDK level also strips Read/Glob/Grep so the turn cannot wander.

Also: the frame-action allowlist.

title: Two named agents with a shared seed builder
description: `buildSeedFor` is shared between the board's Ask action and `resolveAgent`, so the two entry points **cannot drift**. Two ways in, one definition of what the agent knows.

title: src/matchpage.ts — the deterministic match page
description:
## The starting-XI trap

Do **not** build a section with eleven seats. The failure mode is backwards: 3,556 team-games flag exactly 11 starters, **674 flag more (up to 22)**, and only 45 flag fewer. A section designed for eleven would render eighteen.

Cap at 11 by minutes and surface the overflow as a warning badge — catching the defect that actually occurs.

title: bin/collect-race.ts and race-history.jsonl
description: `race-history.jsonl` is appended once per **observation** — not per collector tick, or the week-over-week arrows lie. The heartbeat re-runs collectors every 30 seconds; an arrow that says "+3 since last week" must be measured against last week's observation, not against the last tick.

title: src/broadsheet.ts — the Sunday dispatch
description:
Teal survives here, because HTML pages can use literal hex — unlike board charts. `--us #0D9488` is Harding and only Harding; `--them #F97316` (dark) / `#EA580C` (light) is the opponent, always.

Keelson's own `validateCategoricalPalette` was run against the Ed Insights hexes: dark passes all four checks (lightness band, chroma floor, colorblind separation ΔE 59.4 protan, surface contrast); light mode warns on `#F97316` at 2.80:1 on white, so light mode swaps to brand-accent `#EA580C`. That is the only adjustment the palette needs.

title: src/sim.ts — the Monte Carlo
description: Shrunk scoring rates over the remaining fixtures. Do not run it before conference play has produced enough matches for the shrinkage to mean something — early-season odds computed off three games are noise presented as insight.

title: Parse SideArm play-by-play — 59,844 substitutions discarded (gh-28)
description:
GitHub issue #28.

## Mechanism

Substitutions are **not** a StatCrew-only feature of the source — they are a StatCrew-only feature of our parser. `packages/pipeline/src/sidearm_parser.py:12` documents tables 8-9 as "Play-by-play (not used for structured data)", and `parse_sidearm_game` builds events only from the scoring summary (:469) and the cautions table (:474). There is no PBP branch at all.

## Value

59,844 substitution events would make minutes-played and starting-XI analysis real rather than inferred. Feeds S8's goal-timing work.

Enhancement, not a correctness defect — sequenced after v1.

title: ctx.registerRegion follow/unfollow with identity-hue allocation
description: Per-team panels created on demand, with hue allocation **and release** — a followed team gets a stable identity colour, and unfollowing returns it to the pool.

title: Content-derived game_id (D-09)
description:
## The problem

When a late-published box score reshuffles `enumerate()` order, old rows stay in Postgres as **phantom fixtures**. The canon stops boards double-counting and the stability check alarms, but anything reading base tables outside the canon still picks them up — and by November that is dozens.

## Why a sweeper was rejected

A sweeper is destructive in someone else's database; a soft-delete column is an alembic ownership problem. Fix the cause upstream instead of cleaning up after it.

## Cost

Content-derived IDs require a one-time full reload. That is why this is deferred to S8 rather than done during S0.5 — it is the right fix, at the wrong moment.

title: bin/collect-form.ts — form strips and goal-timing segments
description: The kind of thing this surfaces: five of eleven Harding goals come after the 75th minute; last year the split was even. That is computable today from 22,754 parsed clocks and nothing has ever asked.

title: S8 — Form, the clock, per-team panels, game_id fix
description:
Goal-timing segments over the 22,754 parsed event rows **no endpoint has ever aggregated**. Then the deferred D-09 correctness work.

Spec: docs/specs/touchline-rib.md#S8.

title: S9 — Post-season and deferred correctness
description:
In November the Race board flips to a clinch/eliminate grid, then a bracket. By December the Press Box holds ~24 observations, 14 dispatches, ~130 match pages, and a staircase chart of the season's scraping — flat steps and all.

Then the correctness work that genuinely needed deferring.

Spec: docs/specs/touchline-rib.md#S9.

title: Bracket mode and the season-in-review page
description: The Race region flips to clinch/eliminate, then to a bracket. The Dispatch splits into preview/review pairs.

title: The caution Type column at sidearm_parser.py:339-348
description: So red cards become visible outside Harding. Sequenced after the S0.5 offline backfill (T-red-cards), which recovers the historical 166 — this makes new ones parse correctly going forward.
close_reason: Folded into tl-9ap. Splitting the parser change from the backfill was wrong on two counts: D-03 explicitly moved the sidearm_parser.py:339-348 Type-column fix into the S0.5 repair pass (the S9 sentence in the spec is the overruled side of a spec self-contradiction), and scheduling it post-season would store every 2026 red card as yellow while making tl-4jg's '0 field diffs' gate unsatisfiable. tl-9ap now covers the parser change plus the re-parse backfill as one change.

title: The sidearm_legacy scraper — so NSU stops being reconstructed
description:
NSU's site is a KnockoutJS SPA and needs a headless browser. Until this lands, NSU's overall record is not recoverable — only their conference record, reconstructed from the six schools they played (D-06).

This is the honest fix for the one place where the boards currently have to caveat themselves.
